results.reason: Frontmatter lacks explicit question_count field; body contains roughly 15 attorney-directed questions across two lists, consistent with post's stated focus
Post makes procedural/common-knowledge claims (jail calls recorded, social media subpoenaed) rather than specific stats or case citations requiring inline sourcing
Action items use plain language ('open your phone's notes app', 'scan your social media', 'start the folder') well within 10th grade level
None of the flagged cliches (end of the day, tip of iceberg, slippery slope, double-edged sword, game changer, wake-up call) appear in the post
Consistently uses 'you' and 'your loved one' throughout; brief third-person phrasings never run 2+ consecutive sentences
Predominantly active construction; passive usage ('is recorded', 'is being filed') stays well under 30% threshold
Arraignment, indigent, diversion program, and subpoena are used without inline definitions (3+ undefined legal terms)
Logical problem→context→solution→action flow: role definition, jail call rules, finding a lawyer, mistakes to avoid, first meeting prep, CTA close
Multiple actionable CTAs: Family Member Case Research product link, Defense Milestone Score, 'Right now' action items in every section
Action statements are direct imperatives ('Stop', 'Write the answers down', 'Print the charging documents'); hedging reserved for information claims
No paragraph exceeds 300 words; action-oriented 'Right now' paragraphs stay under 100 words each
Six main sections share word count roughly evenly; no section approaches 50% of total
Every threat (jail call evidence, witness tampering, social media subpoena, burnout) is paired with a specific action within 1-2 sentences per Witte EPPM
Opens with 3AM kitchen scenario hook, middle builds case with concrete rules and examples, closes empowering reader with folder-prep action and product CTA

results.evidence: Post contains direct legal-action directives phrased as commands: 'Do not talk to the victim to work it out,' 'Do not talk to the cops to explain,' 'Do not post on social media,' and 'take it down' for existing posts.

Decision/action sections consistently redirect to attorneys — jail call section uses 'We'll talk about that with the lawyer. Not now.'; mistakes section includes 'I'd like to speak with an attorney'; first-meeting section is entirely attorney-focused.
Post speaks to a general family-member role and never evaluates the reader's specific case strength or likely outcome.
No specific motions, suppression requests, continuances, or subpoenas are recommended as reader actions.
Post does not discuss immigration consequences (no mention of deportation, visa, DACA, or green card), so the immigration-specific redirect requirement does not trigger.
Post does not mention specific collateral consequences (firearm rights, voting rights, housing, professional licensing, student loans), so no sourcing gap exists.
Only general categories are used ('a public defender,' 'a private attorney,' 'State Bar Referral Service') — no specific firm, bail bond company, or provider is named with a recommendation.
No instances of 'we recommend,' 'we advise,' or 'we suggest' in a legal-action context appear in the post.
Rhetorical scene-setting like 'You are standing in the kitchen at 6 AM' is emotional framing, not a legal-facts hypothetical that could be confused with a real case.
Post explicitly frames the reader's role as support: 'Your job is to gather, research, and protect. Not to play lawyer,' and lists 'Trying to play lawyer' as a top mistake.
Qualifiers are used throughout — FAQ uses 'Generally no' and 'Not always'; PD section uses 'Some PD offices are excellent and some are crushed'; diversion described as 'may be considered.'
Outcome language is qualified — 'sometimes waiting 24-48 hours... reduces the amount' uses 'sometimes,' and attorney selection advice says to avoid anyone who 'promises an outcome.'
Post describes general defensive behaviors and procedural categories (PD vs private vs referral) rather than presenting novel legal strategies requiring attribution.
No internally contradictory legal claims appear — charge categories, call-recording rules, and representation options are each described consistently.

Family Member Case Research is framed as a 'briefing' with 'questions to bring to the attorney meeting,' and the Score tool is called 'a starting point for the conversation you're about to have with an attorney' — both positioned as preparation, not substitution.

Opening names the fear in first 2 sentences ('Your brother got arrested last night...You're the one who can't eat') and H2s like 'Finding a Lawyer Without Getting Ripped Off' and 'What To Bring To The First Attorney Meeting' are action-oriented.

Multiple legal terms used without inline definition: 'indigent', 'witness tampering', 'power of attorney', 'diversion program', 'arraignments', and 'pretrial resolution' all appear without dash/parenthetical definitions.
No immediate-action block exists before the first H2 — the pre-H2 content is narrative framing and the TLDR's 'Your Next Step' points to the paid product, not a 5-minute free action.

The 'Finding a Lawyer' section presents three representation options (PD, private, referral service) without naming a default path; the filter sentence about 'answers clearly' comes later and doesn't resolve which of the three to pursue first.

Multiple sections exceed 3 unranked items: the 'what you CAN do' list has 6 bullets, 'Questions to ask any lawyer' has 8 unranked items, and the folder contents list has 7 items — none marked with 'start with these' priority.
This post uses the system-decoder-post pattern — decoding the unspoken role of 'family case manager' into rules, mistakes, and a meeting-prep system.

Threats are consistently paired with actions: the recorded-calls threat pairs with the 'We'll talk about that with the lawyer. Not now.' rule, and the witness-tampering warning pairs with 'I'd like to speak with an attorney before I answer any questions.'
Zero blame language — the 'Biggest Mistakes' section explicitly reframes with 'Not because you are careless, but because nobody told you the rules,' separating person from situation.

Opening validates fear and middle reduces unknown to known, but the final sentence is a generic CTA ('Take the free Defense Milestone Score on their behalf — 10 questions, instant results') rather than an agency statement to the reader.
No tables, only H2 headings used, key actions are bolded, and each H2 section appears to fit within the 300-500 word target without H4+ nesting.

Four H2 sections have strong screenshot sentences (e.g., 'The most common way families hurt a case is by trying to help without knowing the rules'), but 'What To Bring To The First Attorney Meeting' and 'What This Post Can't Do' lack a bolded shareable sentence.

Q1 runs 5 sentences (borderline long) and Q4 ('Public defenders are licensed criminal defense attorneys appointed when the defendant qualifies as indigent') opens in institutional-explainer voice rather than support-group peer voice.
